chose: One strike family for the study nudge's browsers and the Jobs notice's phones, built once in file_host::strikes (SET_ASIDE_AFTER = 3, PROBE_EVERY_HOURS = 24). (1) Storage: columns strikes, set_aside_at, set_aside_why (timeouts, no_answer, sender_mismatch, refused) and last_probe_at on push_subscriptions and jobs_notice_device, not a shared table. (2) Per-sender closed strike sets, where a strike is only the device's own failure. Web push: a delivery timeout or no answer, held for the pass and taken at its end only if some push service answered in that pass (Reach, nudge/deadline.rs); never 400 (our payload or VAPID JWT), 403 (our key), 413, 429, 5xx, a send never made, or a timeout the pass deadline cut short. A pass whose only send is to one dead browser takes no strike, so a lone browser is set aside only across passes that also reached another push service. FCM: 403 SENDER_ID_MISMATCH, and a 400 only when another phone took the same notice in that pass; never 401, a token-endpoint refusal or a JWT home could not sign (fcm_kit's NoToken; its 429 or 5xx is tried again later, not refused), 429, 5xx or no answer, so a lone phone's 400 never strikes. A phone is probed and takes at most one strike per pass. (3) A set-aside device is included at most once a day, only in a send that happens anyway: accepting brings it back (strikes = 0), failing leaves it aside with no new strike and no new set-aside count, and registering again also brings it back. A subject whose browsers are all set aside and probed within the day is not claimed; one whose daily probe is due is claimed, and the due nudge is its probe. (4) A Jobs notice is owed to a phone that registered before the record's window closed and was not set aside at or before the record started; a record no phone was sent is not recorded as told, and one past its window that no phone was owed is closed as skipped, so a phone that comes back later can't make it a loss. A phone that comes back between a record's window closing and the next pass does make that record owed, and lost. Setting one aside is counted once (study-nudge/device_set_aside, jobs-notice/phone_set_aside). A device is set aside after 3 strikes in a row: the owner said 'a few timeouts' on server#1180, and 3 is the coordinator's starting value for 'a few', part of this call. That a device is set aside rather than deleted, and that a delivery it accepts later or registering again brings it back, is the coordinator's elaboration on server#1180, not the owner's words.
options: Columns on each device table, per-sender closed strike sets guarded against home's own failures, and a once-a-day inclusion only within real sends
A shared device_strikes table keyed by endpoint or token, which holds an endpoint or a token a second time (docs/identity.md)
Forget a phone on FCM error codes as UNREGISTERED does: a payload bug of ours reads as INVALID_ARGUMENT and would forget every phone (ruled out on server#1222)
Re-registration as the only way back, so the coordinator's rule on server#1180 that a delivery accepted later brings a device back could never happen, since a set-aside device is never sent to
A scheduled probe, which is a clock (docs/home-compute.md)

Strike a web push timeout only when another device in the same send answered: safe in an outage, but narrower than the chosen 'any push service answered in the pass', which also counts another browser's or subject's send
gray: Whether a failure is the device's or home's can't always be told: a lone phone's FCM 400 may be its token or our notice, so it never strikes, and server#1222 stays open for a single-phone owner except on SENDER_ID_MISMATCH. And a record that started at or after the moment every phone was set aside is owed to none, so it is not counted lost: setting each phone aside was the count. The owner's words cover timeouts only. Striking on a phone's own FCM refusals (SENDER_ID_MISMATCH, a 400 beside a phone that took the notice) is the coordinator's reading on server#1222; striking on web push's no answer is this call's own. Neither is the owner's. The outage guard has a cost the owner may not want: a single-browser owner's passes reach no other push service, so that browser is never struck for timeouts and the owner's 'after a few timeouts' does not apply to it, as a lone phone's FCM 400 never strikes.
